body:
VaneFS repeats SQL parsing for individual 4 KiB blocks, synchronizes inode-reference bookkeeping, and performs directory and checkpoint work in I/O requests. This PR reduces that work and adds an explicit fsync durability mode plus an opt-in Linux SQLite fdatasync build. The production 4 KiB SQLite BLOB format and strict FULL-commit default remain unchanged.

Reuse connection-local prepared statements and read visible blocks through an ordered range join. Complete-block writes skip preliminary payload reads; vacant intervals batch at most 64 nonzero blocks per payload/version insert. Occupied intervals retain version splitting, unchanged-content reuse and the rowid-limit fallback. Content and metadata updates remain atomic.

Under the exclusive writable-branch lease, cache positive FUSE entries and attributes for 60 seconds and invalidate changed attributes. Persist inode pins on first/last reference, with intermediate counts tracked transactionally per connection. Capture directory entries and attributes on first read and preserve the list across pagination and rewind, including unlink and GC.

Add `--durability=fsync`, C++ `Durability::Fsync` and `Workspace::Sync()`. Ordinary mutations commit under NORMAL for cross-handle visibility. File/directory fsync and fdatasync, O_SYNC/O_DSYNC writes and explicit workspace close use FULL barriers; ordinary file close is not a durability barrier. Fsync connections checkpoint on a separate connection after 16 MiB of committed WAL, apply restart admission at 64 MiB and retain 16 MiB on reuse. FULL barriers bypass admission. Background errors, failed-close retries, reader contention and fork/crash recovery remain explicit. Live direct I/O and disabled kernel writeback remain unchanged.

The optional `x64-linux-fdatasync-release` triplet builds SQLite with `HAVE_FDATASYNC=1` using a separate SDK/cache identity. A two-entry CI matrix exercises both variants with actual-syscall expectations and sanitizer coverage. `VANE_FS_TEST_SQLITE_SYNC` selects the expected syscall in the native test; it does not change runtime durability. The default SDK is unchanged. See the [build instructions](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/README.md#optional-linux-sqlite-fdatasync-build).

[Production measurements](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/benchmarks/CHECKPOINT_OPTIMIZATION.md) retain configurations, samples and durability checks. The [partial-write acceptance](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/benchmarks/partial_write/acceptance/README.md) compares fixed-buffer native and FUSE workloads on tmpfs and ext4. That candidate remains isolated: unaligned native write CPU falls by 26.5–28.4%, but the complete physical-storage window fails its frozen gates. The [checkpoint-priority evaluation](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/benchmarks/checkpoint_priority/README.md) also remains isolated: a shorter mutex wait transfers work into foreground RESTART without improving whole admission. No production threshold or scheduling policy changes.

The [external partial-edge evaluation](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/benchmarks/staged_payload/partial_edges/README.md) identifies a separate allocation cliff in the format-1004 prototype. A partially occupied edge sends otherwise vacant new blocks through individual 4 KiB BLOB inserts. The C++ candidate batches vacant subintervals, includes a partial edge only when its full replacement interval is vacant, and preserves automatic/explicit payload-ID ordering and publication guards. For the separately instrumented 32 MiB split-write diagnostic, live external references rise from 12.45% to 99.61%, and WAL syscall bytes fall from 36.60 to 5.00 MiB (86.3%). These counts are not physical-device write amplification.

All six alternating pairs are retained in each fresh/GC-aged state and on both media, totaling 48 independent mounts. First-256-MiB ext4 median throughput improves from 62.48 to 156.05 MiB/s, but aggregate throughput including every fsync/close and slow sample is 62.42 to 68.86. GC-aged aggregate improves from 63.40 to 113.10. Fresh ext4 wins only four of six pairs and request p99 grows from 0.335 to 0.921 seconds; aged tmpfs small writes and some ext4 control workloads also miss the frozen gates. The external format and candidate remain experimental. Timings alone do not locate each remaining stall or attribute it to another workload; the host owner confirms this is a dedicated machine.

The [payload-sync diagnosis and early-writeback evaluation](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/benchmarks/staged_payload/partial_sync/README.md) isolates the remaining stalls in experimental format 1004. A separate 16-mount diagnostic captures a 3.623-second payload fdatasync during a subsequent large write and overlapping publication-lock waits. An isolated C++ candidate submits contiguous payload ranges with WRITE-only hints at 16 MiB, retains the description through publication, and preserves the original whole-file data barrier before FULL WAL commit. Unsupported calls fall back, EINTR retries and I/O/space errors propagate.

The complete 48-mount plain comparison uses the preceding partial-edge candidate as control. Fresh ext4 combined 256 + 64 MiB throughput falls from 66.29 to 61.67 MiB/s despite a faster first phase; the subsequent phase has a 6.173-second final fsync. GC-aged combined throughput rises from 47.04 to 67.69 MiB/s but wins only three of six pairs, and random-overwrite and other gates also fail. A subsequent 8-mount diagnostic records all 92 real WRITE-only hints. One first-write phase spends 4.738 of 7.091 seconds in submission, including a 1.057-second call sampled in rq_qos_wait. This directly locates foreground submission as another blocking path. The writeback candidate is rejected and remains isolated.

The [background payload-writeback evaluation](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/benchmarks/staged_payload/background_writeback/README.md) moves WRITE-only submission to a dedicated C++ thread with one active and one coalesced pending range. It opens the error observer before external append, preserves the whole-payload barrier before FULL WAL commit, reports asynchronous errors, and handles failed-close retry, worker restart, fork and GC. Forced-blocking tests prove writes, reads and final synchronization can progress while submission remains blocked; the same fixture rejects the preceding foreground implementation.

All 48 plain mounts retain six alternating pairs per medium/state. Fresh ext4 combined 256 + 64 MiB throughput is 85.46 to 82.48 MiB/s (4/6 wins); after-GC throughput is 68.86 to 73.89 (3/6 wins). Sixteen frozen checks fail, including random overwrites, small-file fsync and lifecycle. The candidate remains isolated. A separate eight-mount diagnosis records 88 successful hints on distinct threads; a coalesced 48 MiB request blocks for 2.480 seconds, a subsequent-write payload barrier takes 3.604 seconds, and a small-file phase spends 6.091 seconds in WAL synchronization. Short spans below 1 ms are filtered and reported as bounds. Intervals overlap; they do not establish hints as the sole cause of every remaining tail.

The separate [single-block query evaluation](https://github.com/AstroVela/vane/blob/492e580b2aad045c28df36b7d08ee5bd575fdc29/vane_fs/benchmarks/point_read/README.md) preserves equality-query candidates for BLOB and external controls without enabling either. Old-snapshot CPU improves by 9.4% and 6.3%, below the predeclared 10% requirement, and complete FUSE nonregression gates also fail. Multi-block SQL and production sources are unchanged.

Validation:

- The background candidate passes 154 related Python tests (one unsupported v1 migration skip), both variants' 11 native suites, all 11 candidate suites under ASan/UBSan, and 17 dedicated cases in Release and sanitized builds. Dedicated cases cover blocked progress, coalescing, error fallback/retry, failed-close worker restart, fork, GC, late errors and cold recovery after process exit with a blocked hint. All 56 plain/diagnostic mounts validate content, stop and unmount; 198 owned data paths are removed. Split samples regenerate the exact frozen-gate decision, the patch reconstructs all 35 native/test/Python source files, and 660 retained artifact identities verify.
- The preceding foreground-writeback candidate passes 154 related Python tests (one unsupported production-v1 migration skip), both plain variants' 11 native suites, all 11 candidate suites under ASan/UBSan, and nine additional hint/error/order cases in Release and sanitized builds. All 72 diagnostic/plain mounts validate their content and cleanup. Published split samples regenerate the exact frozen-gate decision; 649 retained artifact identities verify. Release fault helpers and four diagnostic mount programs reconstruct byte-identically; the formatted sanitized helper repeats all nine cases successfully.
- The preceding external partial-edge candidate passes 154 related Python tests (one explicit unsupported production-v1 migration skip), 11 native component suites, and the same 11 suites under ASan/UBSan. The native control passes all 11. Staging covers 66 software crash/loss cases, including 33 new partial-edge cases and SQL spilling before external publication. These are software fault tests, not physical power-loss certification.
- All 48 partial-edge mounts pass their content, retained-guard and format checks. All raw request vectors and scalar results are published in split JSON files; generated databases and payload sidecars are removed after owned processes stop and mounts disappear. The published patch reconstructs the exact measured native/test source bytes, and 297 retained artifact identities verify.
- The read-query candidates pass 136 BLOB and 148 external Python tests, with one external format-migration skip, plus their native suites and bounded-version-scan regressions. Their 72 plain native trials and 48 FUSE mounts retain every sample and content check. Nine diagnostic/probe programs reconstruct byte-identically; 766 retained artifact identities verify.
- Only related tests run. No owned builds or correctness tests overlap plain measurement windows. Production source, installed component and SQLite SDK hashes remain unchanged. Affected-file formatting, hooks and copyleft checks pass. No kernel, device, scheduler or global-cache setting changes.

Follow-up to #964, based on its merged main commit.
